title: Graceful inflight prefetch + lease deallocation for safe KV reclamation
creator: Ryan Chen
description: Problem: under continuous batching and aggressive GPU memory compaction we observed correctness issues where in-flight requests referenced KV slots that were reclaimed mid-request. This ticket introduces a graceful deallocation protocol that combines short leases, prefetch fencing, and tombstone markers to guarantee liveness and linearizability for prefix-aware KV reclamation while preserving low tail latency. The goal is an approach that interoperates with LRU and TTL heuristics, integrates with the existing batching router, and adds bounded memory overhead.
background: We run hundreds of concurrent model streams with continuous batching and KV prefix caching. To reduce fragmentation and free memory we currently run TTL-based sweeps + opportunistic LRU trimming. However, with high concurrency and long-generation sequences we saw rare but reproducible failures: tokens generated referencing stale KV entries or causing OOMs because reclamation raced with active KV lookups. Existing tickets focused on eviction correctness proofs and lifetime invariants but did not address prefetch/inflight interactions and GPU allocator fragmentation patterns for small prefetched slices.
proposal_summary: Implement lease-based fencing for in-flight KV usage: when a request prefetches or pins a prefix slice it obtains a short-lived lease (milliseconds to seconds depending on model length). Eviction marks the slice as tombstoned and begins asynchronous reclamation only after all leases expire or are explicitly released. For long-running generations, callers can renew leases or extend pinned ranges. Integrate lease checks into the continuous batching path to avoid adding per-token round-trips. Provide fallbacks: immediate read-copy for rare races and deterministic fallback to a lower-capacity model variant when memory pressure is high.
acceptance_criteria: No observed correctness regressions in production fuzzing harness (0 failures in 1M simulated request sequences)
End-to-end p99 generation latency increase < 5% for typical workloads (measured on dedicated perf cluster)
Memory reclaimed within configured grace window after last active lease expires
Automated linearizability tests present in runtime test-suite and passing in CI
Telemetry surfaces lease wait counts, tombstone churn, and reclaimed bytes by prefix
design_notes: Lease format: (prefix_id, slice_id, epoch, expiry_ts). Leases are cheap 8-16 byte tokens attached to batched requests.
Tombstone lifecycle: tombstone -> drain_wait -> reclaimable. Drain_wait is max(lease_grace, ttl_tail_margin)
Batching integration: lease issuance occurs at prefetch aggregation point; a single batched lease covers multiple request contexts for the same prefix within the batch window
Allocator considerations: avoid immediate slab compaction for tombstoned slices — mark for delayed slab consolidation pass during low-util periods
Fallbacks: read-copy creates a transient copy of slice data to satisfy inflight readers when reclamation is imminent
Compatibility: works with LRU counters by decrementing effective weight only after tombstone enters reclaimable state
decisions: Use short leases (default 500ms) with dynamic extension heuristics based on sequence length and model type
Tombstone retention window = max(lease_grace, 2 * median_request_latency) to bound races under tail spikes
Expose lease metrics and a config knob in Console to tune per-customer defaults
Do not change public API; all lease management is internal to runtime and router
implementation_steps: 1) Add lease token generation and attach to batched prefetch unit (runtime/kernel change)
2) Extend KV metadata with tombstone and epoch fields; add atomic state transition ops
3) Modify eviction worker to mark tombstones and defer reclamation until drain condition
4) Integrate with allocator to perform delayed slab compaction and record reclaimed metrics
5) Add read-copy fastpath for race resolution
6) Add unit/integration/fuzz tests and CI gates
7) Run canary on dedicated perf cluster, collect metrics, roll out gradually
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease issuance, expiry, and explicit release
Fuzz harness that simulates continuous batching with random prefetch/evict interleavings (target 1M sequences) — integrate into nightly CI
Property-based linearizability tests verifying read-after-evict semantics
End-to-end perf runs on perf-cluster-3 comparing p50/p95/p99 latency and memory churn against baseline
Load test with synthetic long generations to exercise lease-renewal path
Canary rollout telemetry dashboard (lease_waits, tombstone_count, reclaim_rate, fallback_rate)
rollout_plan: Dark-launch on 10% of traffic in dedicated perf cluster for 72 hours
Enable on non-critical customers and run 7-day soak
If metrics stable, enable for all hosted API traffic with monitoring alert thresholds
Post-rollout: run a 2-week regression sweep and then remove feature flag if stable
metrics_and_alerts: lease_wait_count per-minute > threshold -> pager (possible config bug)
